judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are BASIC 5 Indicators (rank 1, same grain) under the same Content Standard B5.1.1.1 ('quantities and place value for multi-digit numerals') in Strand 1 Number, Sub-strand Counting, Representation & Cardinality. B5.1.1.1.3 asks learners to identify numbers in different positions around a given number in a number chart (relative position/number-sense), while B5.1.1.1.5 asks learners to round off/up/down whole numbers up to 100,000 to the nearest ten thousands, thousands, hundreds and tens; the LCs confirm these distinct skill sets (number chart/position tags vs rounding/place value tags). They are substantively coherent as complementary place-value and number-sense skills within the same standard, but the evidence does not substantiate a dependency: chart-position identification is not shown to be required or clearly supportive preparation for the rounding procedure, and the two share only the generic token 'numbers' (jaccard 0.04) plus weak code-prefix and adjacent-page signals, which alone carry no semantic weight. Same rank offers no directional warrant, so the symmetric relatesTo is the supported judgment. Evidence is bounded: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and the parent Content Standard carries a merged 'stale B5.1.1.1 CONT'D' audit note, which does not alter the indicator texts relied on here.

judgment.rationale: Both are Indicator-grain statements at the same resolved BASIC 6 coordinate (rank 2) within Strand 1: Number, Sub-Strand 2: Number Operations. The first (B6.1.2.3.1, under Content Standard B6.1.2.3 'Manipulate numbers, using basic division fact up to 144') is recall/determination of basic division facts up to 81; the second (B6.1.2.4.1, under Content Standard B6.1.2.4 'Demonstrate understanding of division of a 2 or 3-digit number by a 1 or 2-digit number') requires dividing 3-digit numbers by a 1-digit number 'efficiently'. Same-rank direction is supported by substantive content evidence, not mere code/page proximity: fluency with basic division facts is the computational substrate that makes efficient multi-digit division by a 1-digit divisor attainable, so proficiency in the first supports success in the second. LC tag overlap ('division') and shared ancestry are corroborating only. Source evidence excerpts for both endpoints are truncated (24 omitted items each), so exemplar detail is unavailable; the statement texts themselves are sufficient for this judgment.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are BASIC 6 Content Standards (same statement-type grain) at the same configured coordinate rank 2, placed in different strands: B6.1.2.5 under Strand 1 Number / Sub-Strand 2 Number Operations ('Translate word problems into mathematical sentences and solve') and B6.2.3.1 under Strand 2 Algebra / Sub-Strand 3 Variables and Equations ('Solve problems involving single-variable, one-step equations with whole number coefficients.'). They share substantive, pair-specific instructional coherence: each requires learners to render a worded situation as a symbolic mathematical statement and then solve it, so work on translating and solving word problems meaningfully reinforces, and is reinforced by, forming and solving one-step single-variable equations. This is more than the generic shared tokens 'solve'/'problems', the shared 'b6' code segment, or the shared BASIC 6 Grade ancestor, none of which alone would justify a relation. A developmental claim is not warranted: the two standards sit at the same rank in parallel strands, the bounded context for B6.1.2.5 points to multi-step four-operation arithmetic word problems while B6.2.3.1 addresses a narrower one-step equation form, and the evidence does not establish which proficiency supports success in the other, so relatesTo with null direction is the supported judgment.
